get.description:
Returns historical (time-series) HAProxy metrics for a load balancer, sourced from Prometheus. The metric is selected by the `metric_name` query parameter and the look-back window by `interval` (in seconds). Frontend metrics return data for the load balancer's frontend; backend metrics return data for the backend named by the `server` parameter.

The HTTP response-code metrics (`haproxy_backend_http_responses_total`, `haproxy_frontend_http_responses_total`) return the current value bucketed by response class - `labels` is `["2xx","3xx","4xx","5xx"]` and `results` holds the matching counts. All other metrics return a range series over `interval`. See `metric_name` for the full list of metrics the console requests.

parameters.name: lb_id
parameters.description: The `id` of the load balancer, as returned by the List Load Balancers endpoint.
x-constraints: must be a valid load balancer (appliance) ID

parameters.name: metric_name
parameters.description: Name of the HAProxy/Prometheus metric to fetch. The backend does not restrict this to a fixed enum (any metric the HAProxy exporter publishes will work), but the console requests the specific frontend and backend metrics listed below. Defaults to `haproxy_backend_http_responses_total`.
x-constraints: backend metrics requested by the console: haproxy_backend_http_responses_total, haproxy_backend_bytes_in_total, haproxy_backend_bytes_out_total, haproxy_backend_current_queue, haproxy_backend_max_queue, haproxy_backend_current_sessions, haproxy_backend_sessions_total, haproxy_backend_limit_sessions, haproxy_backend_max_sessions, haproxy_backend_up, haproxy_backend_response_errors_total, haproxy_backend_connection_errors_total, haproxy_backend_current_session_rate, haproxy_backend_max_session_rate

frontend metrics requested by the console: haproxy_frontend_http_responses_total, haproxy_frontend_max_session_rate, haproxy_frontend_limit_session_rate, haproxy_frontend_current_sessions, haproxy_frontend_max_sessions, haproxy_frontend_limit_sessions, haproxy_frontend_sessions_total, haproxy_frontend_request_errors_total, haproxy_frontend_requests_denied_total, haproxy_frontend_bytes_in_total, haproxy_frontend_bytes_out_total, haproxy_frontend_current_session_rate
any metric name containing "frontend" is queried with frontend labels; otherwise backend labels are used

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Look-back window in seconds for the time-series query. Defaults to 3600 (1 hour).

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: Name of the backend to scope backend metrics to. Defaults to the load balancer's first backend.
x-constraints: must match an existing backend name on the load balancer

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the project to scope the request to. Required integer project ID.
x-constraints: must be a valid integer project ID

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: API key used to authenticate the request

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Region of the load balancer.

schema.description: For the HTTP response-code metrics, `labels` holds the response classes and `results` the matching counts. For range metrics, `labels` holds timestamps and `results` the per-timestamp values.

labels.description: Series labels (response classes for response-code metrics, timestamps for range metrics).

put.description:
Enables or disables shipping of the load balancer's HAProxy access logs to an object-storage (EOS) bucket. The behaviour is controlled by the `is_enabled` query parameter together with the request body:
- **Enable**: call with `?is_enabled=true` and a body containing
  `appliance_id`, `access_key`, `secret_key`, and `bucket` - the
  credentials for the destination object-storage bucket.

- **Disable**: call with a body of `{ "appliance_id": "<id>",
  "disable": true }`.

get.description:
Lists the load balancer plans (SKUs) available to the account in the requested region. Each plan describes the compute backing the load balancer appliance - vCPU, RAM, disk, hourly/monthly price, maximum concurrent connections, and any committed (reserved) pricing options.

Use the `name` of a plan (for example `E2E-LB-2`) as the `plan_name` field when creating or upgrading a load balancer. Plans whose `available_inventory_status` is `false` cannot currently be provisioned in the region.

post.description:
Provisions a load balancer appliance (HAProxy). A single endpoint creates both types - the request body shape is what distinguishes them:

- **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** - Layer-7 (HTTP/HTTPS). Identified by
  one or more `backends` (and no `tcp_backend`). Supports host/path ACL
  routing, SSL termination, WebSocket timeouts, and node-based or
  auto-scaling-group backends. `lb_mode` is `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, or `BOTH`.

- **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** - Layer-4 (TCP). Identified by a single
  `tcp_backend` entry (and no `backends`). `lb_mode` is `TCP` and the
  listening port comes from the `tcp_backend` entry. ACLs and SSL are not
  supported.


`backends` and `tcp_backend` are mutually exclusive. ACL rules (`acl_list` / `acl_map`) are always sent **empty** at create time and added later via the Update Load Balancer endpoint. On success the appliance is returned in `Creating` state - poll the Load Balancer Status endpoint until it becomes `Running`.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the project to scope the request to. Required integer project ID.
x-constraints: must be a valid integer project ID

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: API key used to authenticate the create request

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Region in which the load balancer will be provisioned.
x-constraints: must be a valid region name (e.g., Delhi, Chennai)

schema.description: Create payload for both load balancer types. Send `backends` for an **ALB** (Layer 7) or a single `tcp_backend` for an **NLB** (Layer 4) - the two are mutually exclusive and exactly one is required. ALB-only fields (`ssl_context`, `acl_list`/`acl_map`, per-backend `http_check` / `websocket_timeout` / `backend_ssl`) do not apply to an NLB.

plan_name.description: Plan SKU backing the load balancer appliance. Use the `name` of a plan returned by LB Plans (for example `E2E-LB-2`).
x-constraints: must reference an existing load balancer plan in the region

lb_name.description: Display name of the load balancer.

lb_type.description: Network scheme of the load balancer. `external` exposes a public IP; `internal` is reachable only inside the selected VPC(s) and requires `vpc_list`. (This is the "Scheme/Type" choice in the console; it does **not** distinguish ALB from NLB - the presence of `backends` is what makes this an ALB.)
x-constraints: defaults to external in the console

lb_mode.description: Frontend protocol. For an **ALB**: `HTTP` (port 80 only), `HTTPS` (443 only), or `BOTH` (HTTP redirects honour `ssl_context.redirect_to_https`). For an **NLB**: always `TCP`.
x-constraints: ALB: HTTP | HTTPS | BOTH (console default BOTH); NLB: TCP

lb_port.description: Primary listening port, sent as a string. The console sets `80` when `lb_mode` is `HTTP` and `443` otherwise.
x-constraints: ports 1-1023 and the reserved ports 8080, 10050, 9101 are rejected unless the value is 80 or 443

node_list_type.description: Backend node-list mode. Always `D` (dynamic) for load balancers created from the console.

client_timeout.description: HAProxy client-side inactivity timeout, in seconds.

server_timeout.description: HAProxy server-side inactivity timeout, in seconds.

http_keep_alive_timeout.description: HAProxy HTTP keep-alive timeout, in seconds.

ssl_context.description: TLS configuration. Required when `lb_mode` is `HTTPS` or `BOTH` (an SSL certificate must be selected); not used for plain `HTTP`.

ssl_certificate_id.description: ID of an uploaded SSL certificate to terminate TLS with. Required when `lb_mode` is not `HTTP`; `null` otherwise.
x-constraints: required when lb_mode is HTTPS or BOTH
must reference an SSL certificate owned by the account

redirect_to_https.description: When `true`, plain HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.

backends.description: One or more backend groups the ALB routes traffic to. At least one backend is required for an ALB (this is what distinguishes it from an NLB). `backends` and `tcp_backend` are mutually exclusive.

name.description: Backend group name (also referenced by ACL maps and `default_backend`).

balance.description: Load-balancing (routing policy) algorithm. `source` provides IP stickiness, `roundrobin` distributes evenly, `leastconn` sends to the least-busy server.

backend_ssl.description: Whether the ALB connects to backend servers over HTTPS.

check_url.description: Path used for HTTP health checks.

domain_name.description: Host header used for health checks. The console sends `localhost`.

websocket_timeout.description: WebSocket idle timeout in seconds, or `null` to disable.

network_id.description: VPC network ID for the backend; `null` for public backends.

scaler_id.description: Auto Scaling Group ID when the backend type is an auto-scaling group. `null` for node-based backends.
x-constraints: required when using an auto-scaling-group backend
must reference an active scale group

scaler_port.description: Port on the auto-scaling group's nodes. `null` for node-based backends.
x-constraints: required when using an auto-scaling-group backend

servers.description: Backend servers (nodes) for a node-based backend. Omitted/empty when the backend is an auto-scaling group.

backend_ip.description: Private/public IPv4 address of the backend server.

backend_port.description: Port the backend server listens on.

default_backend.description: Name of the backend that receives traffic not matched by any ACL. May only be set when `backends` is non-empty.
x-constraints: must match one of the `backends[].name` values

acl_list.description: Layer-7 routing rule definitions. Always sent **empty** at create time; add rules afterwards via Update Load Balancer.
x-constraints: send an empty array at create

acl_map.description: Mapping of ACL rules to backends. Always sent **empty** at create time.
x-constraints: send an empty array at create

tcp_backend.description: The single TCP backend group for an **NLB**. Provide exactly one entry for an NLB (and leave `backends` empty); leave this empty for an ALB. `backends` and `tcp_backend` are mutually exclusive.
x-constraints: required for an NLB (exactly one entry); empty for an ALB

port.description: Port the NLB listens on and forwards to the backend servers (also copied to top-level `lb_port`).
x-constraints: ports 1-1023 and the reserved ports 8080, 10050, 9101 are rejected unless the value is 80 or 443

timeout_connect.description: TCP connect timeout in seconds (as a string).

timeout_client.description: TCP client-side timeout in seconds (as a string).

timeout_server.description: TCP server-side timeout in seconds (as a string).

servers.description: Backend servers (nodes) for the TCP backend.

vpc_list.description: VPC(s) the load balancer attaches to. **Required when `lb_type` is `internal`**; optional otherwise.

ipv4_cidr.description: IPv4 CIDR block of the VPC.

subnet_id.description: Subnet ID, when attaching to a specific subnet.

lb_reserve_ip.description: A previously reserved public IPv4 address to assign to the load balancer. Send an empty string to allocate a fresh IP. Not allowed for internal load balancers.
x-constraints: must be a reserved IPv4 address on the account
must be empty when lb_type is internal

is_ipv6_attached.description: Whether to attach a public IPv6 address at creation (external load balancers only).

enable_bitninja.description: Whether to activate the BitNinja security add-on on the appliance.

security_group_id.description: ID of the security group to attach to the load balancer. The console always sends the selected security group.
x-constraints: must reference a security group owned by the account

isEncryptionEnabled.description: Enables disk encryption on the appliance. When `true`, `encryption_passphrase` is required.

encryption_passphrase.description: Passphrase for disk encryption. Only used when `isEncryptionEnabled` is `true`.
x-constraints: must contain at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, and one special character

cn_id.description: Committed (reserved) SKU ID, when creating the load balancer on a committed plan. `null` for standard hourly billing. Use a `committed_sku_id` from LB Plans.

cn_status.description: Committed-plan renewal status. `null` for standard hourly billing.

appliance_id.description: ID of the newly created load balancer.

IP.description: Public IP assigned to the load balancer.

is_credit_sufficient.description: Whether the account had sufficient credit for the request.

put.description:
Updates the configuration of an existing load balancer. This is the endpoint used to add or change backends, backend servers, ACL routing rules (`acl_list` / `acl_map`), the TCP backend (`tcp_backend`), timeouts, SSL settings, and the plan.

**The full configuration context must be re-sent on every update** - the console reads the current `context` object (from List Load Balancers), mutates the arrays it needs to change, and PUTs the entire object back. Any field omitted is treated as cleared. Key rules enforced by the backend:
- `backends` and `tcp_backend` are mutually exclusive; `tcp_backend` may
  contain at most one entry.

- `acl_list` / `acl_map` may only be used on an ALB (they cannot coexist
  with `tcp_backend`).

- `default_backend` may only be set when `backends` is non-empty.
- For an internal load balancer (`lb_type: internal`) `vpc_list` is
  required and `lb_reserve_ip` must be empty.

parameters.name: lb_id
parameters.description: The `id` of the load balancer, as returned by the List Load Balancers endpoint.
x-constraints: must be a valid load balancer (appliance) ID

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the project to scope the request to. Required integer project ID.
x-constraints: must be a valid integer project ID

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: API key used to authenticate the update request

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Region of the load balancer being updated.

schema.description: The complete load balancer configuration context. Read the current `context` from List Load Balancers, change the fields you need, and PUT the whole object back. Fields shared with create (plan, timeouts, ssl_context, vpc_list, backends/servers, security and encryption flags) behave identically; the fields below are the ones most relevant to updates.

lb_name.description: Display name (changing it here renames the load balancer).

lb_type.description: Network scheme. `internal` requires a non-empty `vpc_list` and forbids `lb_reserve_ip`.

lb_mode.description: Frontend protocol (`HTTP`/`HTTPS`/`BOTH` for an ALB, `TCP` for an NLB).

x-constraints: ports 1-1023 and reserved ports 8080, 10050, 9101 rejected unless 80 or 443

plan_name.description: Plan SKU. Changing it here is **not** how you upgrade - use Perform Load Balancer Action with `type: upgrade_plan` instead.

backends.description: ALB backend groups (same item shape as create). Add, edit, or remove backends here. Empty for an NLB. Deleting a backend also prunes any `acl_map` entries that targeted it.

websocket_timeout.description: WebSocket idle timeout (1-100s); send null (not empty string) to disable.

tcp_backend.description: NLB TCP backend (same item shape as create). At most one entry. Mutually exclusive with `backends`.

acl_list.description: Layer-7 ACL **rule definitions** (the match conditions). Only valid on an ALB - cannot coexist with `tcp_backend`. Each entry is paired 1:1 with an `acl_map` entry by `acl_name`.

acl_name.description: Unique name for this ACL rule; referenced by the matching `acl_map` entry.

acl_condition.description: HAProxy match condition. Built in the console from an ACL type (Path / Host / Query Parameter / HTTP Request / Source IP) and a comparison.
x-constraints: must be one of the allowed HAProxy match strings

acl_matching_path.description: The value to match - a path, host, IP/CIDR, query-parameter value, or (for an HTTP-request ACL) a space-separated list of methods such as `GET POST`.

acl_map.description: Maps named ACL rules (from `acl_list`) to the backend that should serve matching traffic. Only valid on an ALB.

acl_name.description: Name of the ACL rule (must match an `acl_list[].acl_name`).

acl_backend.description: Name of the backend group that serves traffic matching this ACL.
x-constraints: must match one of the `backends[].name` values

acl_condition_state.description: When `true` (default) the rule routes to `acl_backend` on a match; `false` negates the condition.

default_backend.description: Backend that serves unmatched traffic. Must be empty if there are no `backends`.

vpc_list.description: VPC attachments (required for internal load balancers).

Returns the `id`, `name`, and `status` (such as `Creating`, `Running`, `Powered off`) plus a `data_monitor` object. Pass the `id` query parameter to scope the response to a single load balancer.

Supported actions: `power_on`, `power_off`, `upgrade_plan`, `rename`. Any other value is rejected with `Invalid Action!`.

x-constraints: must be a valid load balancer (appliance) ID

parameters.name: reserve_ip_required
parameters.description: When `true`, the load balancer's public IP is converted to a reserved IP on the account instead of being released.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the project to scope the request to. Required integer project ID.
x-constraints: must be a valid integer project ID

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: API key used to authenticate the delete request

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Region of the load balancer being deleted.
